name: Respond to and investigate collisions
summary: When a company truck is in a collision, the driver secures the scene and calls dispatch, the on-call safety manager guides the driver by phone and arranges towing, and the driver writes a report. The safety manager then pulls ELD, telematics and camera data, interviews the driver, sends the unit to the shop, passes claims to the claims specialist and decides whether the collision was preventable, with a monthly committee for serious or disputed cases. Most collisions are minor, but files stay open for weeks waiting for police reports and committee meetings, and serious collisions bring police, regulators and lawyers.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees running about 1,190 company power units and 380 owner-operators, with six regional safety managers on an on-call rotation.
baseline.notes: About 25 collisions a month: about two thirds minor and drivable (backing, side-swipes, mirror and fixed-object strikes), about 28% needing a tow or with injury, about 5% serious. About 55% are reported to an insurer; most fall within the deductible.

trigger: A driver reports a collision involving a company or owner-operator truck to dispatch.
end_state: The collision file is closed with a preventability decision, the unit sent for repair, the claim passed to liability claims and the record sent to driver performance.

volume.seasonality: Highest from December to March with snow and ice and in the autumn LTL peak; lowest in summer.

evidence.note: Organisation process map volume; about 0.2 collisions per power unit per year. Author's estimate.

surge.cause: Winter storm or highway closure (snowstorms, freezing rain, mountain pass closures)

evidence.note: Organisation file surge: storms close Highway 401, the Trans-Canada through the Rockies and the Coquihalla several times each winter. Author's estimate.

resources.name: Pickup and delivery truck (day-cab tractor or straight truck)

steps.name: Driver secures the scene and checks for injuries
steps.description: The driver stops, puts on hazard lights and sets out warning triangles, checks for injured people and calls 911 when anyone is hurt, the road is blocked or dangerous goods are leaking. The driver stays at the scene and does not discuss fault.

control.basis: Company collision procedure and provincial highway traffic acts: secure the scene, remain and report

next.condition: weekday daytime, city or linehaul driver

evidence.note: Duty to remain and report under provincial highway traffic acts and company collision procedure; author's knowledge.

steps.name: City dispatcher takes the collision call
steps.description: The terminal's city dispatcher takes the driver's call, runs the collision checklist (injuries, police called, vehicle drivable, dangerous goods, freight on board), reassigns the driver's remaining stops and phones the safety manager.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: After-hours dispatcher takes the collision call
steps.description: At night, on weekends and for truckload drivers, the after-hours dispatcher takes the call, runs the same checklist, notes the location from telematics and pages the on-call safety manager.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Safety manager guides the driver by phone
steps.description: The on-call safety manager calls the driver, tells them which photos to take and what information to exchange from the collision kit, decides whether police must be called, whether the unit needs a tow, and whether US post-accident testing applies, and decides whether to go to the scene.

next.condition: unit not drivable, injury or serious collision

evidence.note: Severity split is the author's estimate; most truck collisions are minor property damage (backing, side-swipes, mirror strikes).

steps.name: Dispatcher arranges tow and recovery
steps.description: The after-hours dispatcher calls the contracted towing company, arranges road service or a second unit to recover the freight and trailer, notifies the customer of delayed freight and books the damaged unit into a shop.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Tow operator clears the scene
steps.description: The towing company reaches the scene, waits for police to release the vehicle, uprights or hooks the unit and tows it to the terminal or a shop. Storms, closed highways and heavy-recovery work lengthen the wait.

next.condition: US tow-away crash with citation, testing required

evidence.note: Tow and recovery times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Safety manager drives to the scene
steps.description: For collisions with serious injury, a fatality, a rollover, a dangerous goods release or a highway closure, the safety manager drives to the scene or the hospital, briefing the vice-president of safety by phone on the way.

evidence.note: Six regional safety managers cover the network; distances are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate at the scene
steps.description: Once police release the scene, the safety manager photographs the vehicles, road and sightlines, records positions and skid marks, collects witness names, checks the driver's condition and secures the dash camera and ELD data.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Driver completes post-accident drug and alcohol test
steps.description: For crashes in the US that meet the federal criteria, the driver goes to a collection site for an alcohol test within eight hours and a drug test within 32 hours, and the safety manager records the reason if a test was late or not done.

control.basis: 49 CFR 382.303 post-accident testing (US operations); company drug and alcohol policy in Canada

evidence.note: Post-accident testing criteria and the 2, 8 and 32 hour limits.

steps.name: Driver writes collision report
steps.description: At the end of the shift the driver fills in the company collision report with a diagram and statement, attaches the photos and the other party's details, and hands it to the terminal or uploads it.

error.defect_description: Report missing details, diagram unclear or statement admits fault.

next.condition: police did not attend and damage is over the provincial reporting threshold

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Driver reports to a collision reporting centre
steps.description: Where police did not attend and damage is over the threshold (in Ontario, $2,000 combined until 2025), the driver takes the unit to a police collision reporting centre within the deadline, has the damage photographed and files a report.

control.basis: Ontario Highway Traffic Act s.199 and equivalent provincial rules on reporting collisions to police

evidence.note: Ontario's reporting threshold was $2,000 of combined damage in 2019-2022 (raised to $5,000 in 2025); from the author's knowledge, regulation text not opened.

steps.name: Open collision file and pull vehicle data
steps.description: The safety manager opens a collision file in the safety system, attaches the driver report and photos, and downloads the ELD record, telematics speed and hard-braking data and any forward camera video for the minutes before the collision.

evidence.note: Dash cameras and telematics were common on large fleets by 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Interview the driver and witnesses
steps.description: The safety manager talks to the driver about speed, following distance, mirrors and what the other road user did, calls witnesses where there are any, and fills gaps in the driver's report.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Send unit for damage appraisal and repair
steps.description: The safety manager sends the collision details to the shop manager so the unit is appraised and a repair order opened, and asks for the estimate the claims specialist will need.

next.condition: third-party damage, injury or company damage over the deductible
in-house only, waiting for police report

evidence.note: Share reported to insurers is the author's estimate given large deductibles.

steps.name: Claims specialist reports the claim
steps.description: The claims specialist reports the collision to the insurer or the third party's insurer, opens a claim with a reserve in the claims log and asks the other party for their insurer details.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for police report
steps.description: The claims specialist orders the police collision report, which can take weeks to be released, and the preventability decision usually waits for it.

evidence.note: Police report release times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide preventability
steps.description: The safety manager reviews the file against the company's preventability standard, which asks whether the driver did everything reasonable to avoid the collision, and records preventable or not preventable with the reasons. Disputed, serious or unusual cases go to the review committee.

evidence.note: Preventability standards based on a reasonable-driver test are common in fleet safety; author's knowledge.

steps.name: Collision review committee confirms the decision
steps.description: At its monthly meeting, a committee chaired by the vice-president of safety with operations and, at unionised terminals, a union representative reviews the file and confirms or changes the preventability decision.

control.basis: Company collision review policy and collective agreement

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Communicate the decision and refer for coaching
steps.description: The safety manager tells the driver and the driver's manager the decision, explains what could have been done differently, and refers preventable collisions to coaching or discipline under the driver performance process.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Record collision in register and check carrier profile
steps.description: The safety analyst enters the collision in the accident register and monthly statistics, and checks how the provincial regulator recorded it on the carrier's safety profile (in Ontario, the CVOR record and its collision points).

control.basis: 49 CFR 390.15 accident register (US operations); provincial carrier profile monitoring

next.condition: Ontario collision with points the carrier judges not preventable

evidence.note: US accident register kept 3 years with date, place, driver, injuries, fatalities and hazardous materials release.

steps.name: Prepare CVOR collision point appeal
steps.description: The safety manager assembles the appeal package for the review panel: driver report with diagram, police reports, CVOR record, court disposition, photos and witness statements, with the fee.

evidence.note: Appeal eligibility, required documents and the $750 fee.

steps.name: Wait for review panel decision
steps.description: The panel reviews the evidence and decides whether the collision was preventable; only a not-preventable finding removes the points from the CVOR record.

evidence.note: Panel role and outcome; timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close collision file
steps.description: The safety manager checks that the decision, coaching referral, repair order and insurance claim reference are recorded and closes the collision file; the insurance claim itself continues in the liability claims process.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Serious collision
exceptions.description: Injury, fatality, rollover or dangerous goods release: the safety manager attends, US testing may apply, police reconstruct the collision and the file goes to the committee and to legal counsel.

exceptions.name: Driver disputes preventability
exceptions.description: The driver, often with the union, disputes a preventable finding and the committee reviews it again.

exceptions.name: CVOR point appeal
exceptions.description: An Ontario collision the carrier judges not preventable carries CVOR points; the carrier appeals to the review panel.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from collision report to closed collision file
benchmarks.population: Collisions at a mid-size Canadian carrier, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Minor collisions close in two to three weeks; files waiting for police reports or the monthly committee take one to three months. Author's estimate; no published figure found.

benchmarks.population: Ontario CVOR Collision Point Review Panel

pain_points.description: Files wait weeks for police reports before preventability can be decided.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: The monthly committee adds up to a month to serious and disputed cases.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Driver reports are often incomplete, so the safety manager reconstructs events from telematics, camera video and interviews.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Winter storms bring several collisions at once while tow operators are stretched and highways are closed.

evidence.note: Organisation file surge estimate.

sources.title: 49 CFR 382.303 Post-accident testing
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Alcohol and drug tests after a fatal crash, or after an injury or tow-away crash in which the driver receives a citation; if the alcohol test is not done within 2 hours the reasons are recorded and attempts stop at 8 hours; drug tests stop at 32 hours with a record of the reasons.

sources.title: 49 CFR 390.15 Assistance in investigations and special studies
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Motor carriers keep an accident register for 3 years after each accident with date, place, driver name, injuries, fatalities and hazardous materials released, plus copies of accident reports required by states or insurers.

sources.title: CVOR Collision Point Review Panel
sources.supports: Ontario carriers may appeal CVOR collision points for reportable collisions in Ontario where no charge was laid or no conviction resulted; the package needs a driver report with diagram, police reports, the CVOR record and court documents; non-refundable fee of $750; requests within twelve months of the collision appearing on the CVOR record; the panel decides preventable or non-preventable and only a non-preventable finding removes points.

assumptions: The role pd-driver stands in for the involved driver in every division (about 45% of collisions are pickup and delivery trucks, 35% truckload and 20% linehaul); the pd-truck resource stands in for the involved power unit.
Safety managers are on an on-call rotation after hours for collisions (shift pattern on_call in this process); the organisation file gives them no shift pattern.
Ontario's police reporting threshold of $2,000 combined damage in 2019-2022 and the National Safety Code collision reporting rules are described from general knowledge; their texts were not opened.
US rules (49 CFR 382.303, 390.15) apply only to collisions in US operations or with US-regulated drivers.
Repair, claim handling and coaching continue in other processes and are not timed here.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's.

Simulated median cycle time (about 22 days) matches the 21-day estimate; the simulated 90th percentile (about 40 days) is below the 60-day estimate because only about 45% of files wait for a police report and a quarter go to the committee. Litigated serious collisions that stay open for months are left to the liability claims process.
